concepts.label: IMRAD Structure
concepts.summary: The Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion organization that frames most empirical research papers.

concepts.label: Abstract Anatomy
concepts.summary: Structured (background, methods, results, conclusions) versus unstructured abstracts and how to read them quickly.

concepts.label: Introduction Section
concepts.summary: How papers establish context, identify a knowledge gap, and state the hypothesis or research question.

concepts.label: Methods Section
concepts.summary: Where study design, population, interventions, outcomes, and analysis plan are reported in reproducible detail.

concepts.label: Results Section
concepts.summary: How participant flow, baseline characteristics, primary outcomes, and secondary outcomes are presented without interpretation.

concepts.label: Discussion Section
concepts.summary: Interpretation of findings, comparison to prior work, limitations, and implications for practice or future research.

concepts.label: Randomized Controlled Trial
concepts.summary: Prospective experiment that randomizes participants to interventions to minimize confounding and establish causality.

concepts.label: Cohort Study
concepts.summary: Observational design that follows exposed and unexposed groups forward in time to compare outcome incidence.

concepts.label: Case-Control Study
concepts.summary: Retrospective design comparing prior exposures between people with an outcome (cases) and matched people without (controls).

concepts.label: Cross-Sectional Study
concepts.summary: Snapshot design measuring exposure and outcome at a single time point to estimate prevalence and associations.

concepts.label: Case Series
concepts.summary: Descriptive report of a sequence of similar cases without a comparison group, useful for hypothesis generation.

concepts.label: Non-Inferiority Trial
concepts.summary: RCT variant designed to show a new intervention is not unacceptably worse than a standard comparator within a pre-specified margin.

concepts.label: Systematic Review
concepts.summary: Structured synthesis of all eligible studies on a question using pre-registered search, screening, and appraisal protocols.

concepts.label: Meta-Analysis
concepts.summary: Quantitative pooling of effect estimates across systematic-review studies, typically with forest plots and heterogeneity statistics.

concepts.label: P-Values and Significance
concepts.summary: Probability of observing data at least as extreme as the sample under the null hypothesis, and the conventional 0.05 threshold.

concepts.label: Confidence Intervals
concepts.summary: Range of plausible values for an estimate at a given coverage level (typically 95%), more informative than a p-value alone.

concepts.label: Effect Sizes
concepts.summary: Magnitude of association expressed as odds ratio, risk ratio, hazard ratio, or mean difference, independent of sample size.

concepts.label: Power and Sample Size
concepts.summary: Probability of detecting a true effect of given magnitude, driving sample-size calculations during study design.

concepts.label: Multiple Testing Correction
concepts.summary: Adjustments such as Bonferroni or false-discovery-rate that control type I error inflation across many simultaneous tests.

concepts.label: Regression Models
concepts.summary: Linear, logistic, and Poisson models that estimate adjusted associations between predictors and outcomes.

concepts.label: Survival Analysis
concepts.summary: Time-to-event methods including Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards regression that handle censoring.

concepts.label: Subgroup Analysis
concepts.summary: Pre-specified or exploratory effect estimates within strata of the population, with attention to interaction tests and multiplicity.

concepts.label: Bias Types
concepts.summary: Systematic errors including selection bias, information (measurement) bias, and confounding that distort study findings.

concepts.label: Confounding vs Mediation
concepts.summary: Distinguishing a third variable that distorts an exposure-outcome relationship from one that lies on the causal pathway.

concepts.label: Internal Validity
concepts.summary: Degree to which a study's design and conduct support causal inference within the studied sample, free of bias.

concepts.label: External Validity / Generalizability
concepts.summary: Extent to which study findings apply to populations, settings, and conditions beyond the sample studied.

concepts.label: Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool
concepts.summary: Domain-based assessment (RoB 2) for randomized trials covering randomization, deviations, missing data, measurement, and reporting.

concepts.label: GRADE Evidence Rating
concepts.summary: Framework that grades certainty of evidence (high/moderate/low/very low) across a body of studies for a clinical recommendation.
